data.title: A small company that walks and paddles.
data.intro: WILDROUTES is a small group of guides who run a few trips a year in mountains and on water. This page says who we are and how we work.

children.text: We started with one summer of hut walks in the Alps for friends and friends of friends. Each year we added a trip we wanted to do ourselves: a fjord paddle, a base camp trek, a week of easy walking for parents. We still run only ten trips, each with eight to twelve people at most.
How we run trips

Groups are small so that you can talk to the guide and everyone fits in a hut or a van. Every trip has the same shape: a first evening to meet, a few days that build, a rest or spare day, and a last day that finishes before lunch so you can travel on.

Each trip page gives the distances, hours on foot or on the water, and where you sleep. If the plan on the page does not match what you want, tell us. We would rather say no than send you home disappointed.
Planning and safety

Guides make the call each morning on where it is safe to go. We carry a first aid kit and a satellite messenger on every trip. We change the route or stay put when the weather says so and we do not charge extra for that.
Licences and insurance

data.intro: Sample wording only. Replace it with your own deposit, payment and cancellation terms before you publish.

children.text: This page is placeholder text so the site has a terms page. It is not a contract and no real company stands behind it.
Holding a place
A place is held once we confirm it by email. Sample deposit: 20 percent of the trip price. Sample balance due: 60 days before the first day.
Changes by you
Sample wording: if you cancel more than 60 days before departure we return your deposit minus a small admin fee. Closer to departure the fee goes up in steps.
Changes by us
Sample wording: if a trip cannot run we offer another date, a credit or a full refund. If weather changes the route on the day, the trip carries on with a new plan and no refund is due.
Insurance
Sample wording: every guest needs travel and medical insurance that covers the activities on the trip. We ask to see the policy before departure.

data.title: Lake Corvane Hut Circuit
data.summary: Seven days between mountain huts above a glacial lake, with short climbs and long lunches.
data.intro: A loop of six walking days from one valley, sleeping in a different hut most nights. Days are five to seven hours on foot with one big climb each day.
data.itinerary:
Day 1|Meet in Corvane village at 4 pm. Kit check, dinner and a short briefing from your guide.
Day 2|Valley path to Rifugio Alzo. 5 hours, 700 m up.
Day 3|Over the Passo Sella Nera to the lake hut. 6 hours, 850 m up, 600 m down.
Day 4|Rest morning by the lake, then an easy ridge walk. 4 hours.
Day 5|Longest day: the glacier moraine path to Rifugio Tre Corni. 7 hours.
Day 6|Down through larch forest to the village of Ponte Alto. 5 hours.
Day 7|Breakfast, then transfer to Corvane by 11 am.
data.includes:
Six nights: two in a village guesthouse, four in mountain huts (shared rooms)
Breakfast and dinner every day, trail lunches on walking days
One guide for up to six walkers, two guides for seven to ten
Transfers between the meeting point and the trailheads
Park and hut-booking fees
data.bring:
Broken-in walking boots
Waterproof jacket and trousers
A 30 to 40 litre daypack
Walking poles
Sheet sleeping bag for the huts
Sun hat, sunglasses and sun cream
Two litres of water capacity

children.text: Who this trip suits
You are comfortable walking all day with a light pack and have done some hill walking before. You do not need mountaineering experience.
What a day is like

We leave the hut around 8 am, stop for lunch at a viewpoint and arrive between 3 and 4 pm. Your main luggage is carried by road to the village on day 1 and 7. For the huts you carry only what you need for four nights.

data.title: Three Passes Trek
data.summary: Nine days crossing three high passes, with two nights in tents and a rest day at a lakeside village.
data.intro: A hard walking trip for people who like long days. Expect up to eight hours on foot and climbs of 1,000 m. Nights alternate between huts and small tents.
data.itinerary:
Day 1|Meet in Serrenta at 5 pm. Briefing and dinner.
Day 2|First pass, Colle dei Fabbri. 7 hours, 1,000 m up.
Day 3|Hut to hut along the Serrenta ridge. 6 hours.
Day 4|Second pass and our first tent camp. 8 hours.
Day 5|Camp to Lago Verro. 6 hours.
Day 6|Rest day at the lakeside village. Swim, wash clothes, sleep.
Day 7|Third pass, Forcella Grigia. 8 hours.
Day 8|Long descent and a last night in a hut. 6 hours.
Day 9|Short walk to the road. Transfer to Serrenta by noon.
data.includes:
Eight nights: five in huts, two in tents, one in a village guesthouse
All meals from dinner on day 1 to lunch on day 9
Tents, sleeping mats and cooking gear for the camp nights
Two guides on every departure
Transfers at the start and end
data.bring:
Broken-in walking boots
Sleeping bag rated to 0 C
A 40 litre pack for camp nights
Walking poles
Warm layer and gloves
Swimwear for the lake rest day

children.text: Fitness
Train for three months before you come. Walk four to six hours with a loaded pack at least once a week, ideally on hills. We send a simple plan after you confirm.
Tent nights
We carry shared tents and food between us. Everyone takes a share of group gear, around three kilos.

data.title: Hardvik Plateau Walk
data.summary: Six easy days across open plateau and fjord edge, with a guesthouse bed every night.
data.intro: Gentle walking on good paths. Days are three to five hours with little climbing, and your bags go ahead by van.
data.itinerary:
Day 1|Meet in Hardvik at 3 pm. Walk the harbour path before dinner.
Day 2|Fjord edge to Skarsnes. 4 hours.
Day 3|Up to the plateau. 5 hours, 450 m up. Picnic by the tarn.
Day 4|Plateau crossing to the old farm at Lundavoll. 4 hours.
Day 5|Down the valley to the waterfall. 3 hours, then a free afternoon.
Day 6|Breakfast and a short walk, then transfer to Hardvik by 1 pm.
data.includes:
Five nights in guesthouses, two people to a room (single room on request)
Breakfast, trail lunch and dinner every day
One guide for up to twelve walkers
Daily luggage transfer by van
Boat ticket on day 2
data.bring:
Walking shoes or light boots
Waterproof jacket
A 20 to 30 litre daypack
Warm hat, light gloves
Swimsuit if you want a cold swim

children.text: Who this trip suits
First-time group travellers, walkers who prefer a bed and a hot shower, and anyone who wants long days outside without a heavy pack.
Light all night
In June it stays light until after 11 pm. Bring an eye mask if that bothers you.

data.title: Silver Pine Lakes Walk
data.summary: Six days of lake loops and wildflower meadows in the Canadian Rockies, with a cabin base.
data.intro: One cabin base for five nights and a different trail each day. Most days are four to five hours with a lake to swim in at the end.
data.itinerary:
Day 1|Meet at the cabins at 4 pm. Walk to the first viewpoint.
Day 2|Silver Pine Lake loop. 4 hours.
Day 3|Meadow trail and the old fire lookout. 5 hours, 500 m up.
Day 4|Free choice: a long walk, a short one, or a canoe on the lake.
Day 5|Ridge trail to Marten Pass. 5 hours.
Day 6|Breakfast, then transfer to the town of Cairnford by 11 am.
data.includes:
Five nights in shared cabins (rooms of two to four)
All meals, cooked in the cabin kitchen by the group
One guide for up to twelve walkers
Park passes
Canoe hire on day 4
data.bring:
Walking boots
Waterproof jacket
Insect repellent
A 20 to 30 litre daypack
Swimsuit and quick-dry towel
Bear spray is carried by guides, so you do not need your own

children.text: Wildlife
Bears and elk live here. Your guide will explain how we walk and what to do if we meet one. We make noise on the trail and keep food in sealed containers.
Cabin life
Each person takes a turn at cooking or washing up. The kitchen has a woodstove and the cabins have electric heaters.

data.title: Ostrevik Fjord Paddle
data.summary: Five days of calm-water sea kayaking in a western Norwegian fjord, camping on small beaches.
data.intro: A first multi-day paddle. Four to five hours on the water each day in sheltered fjord water, with a kayak guide in front and one behind.
data.itinerary:
Day 1|Meet in Ostrevik at 10 am. Boat handling practice in the harbour, then a short paddle to our first beach.
Day 2|Along the north shore to the waterfall. 12 km.
Day 3|Crossing to the island camp. 10 km. Swim and fire if the weather allows.
Day 4|Round the island and up the side fjord. 14 km.
Day 5|Back to Ostrevik by 3 pm. Hot showers at the harbour house.
data.includes:
Four nights camping (tents and mats provided)
All meals from lunch on day 1 to lunch on day 5
Two-person sea kayaks or singles, paddles, spray skirts and buoyancy aids
Dry bags for everyone
Two guides for up to eight paddlers
data.bring:
Warm base layers (no cotton)
Waterproof jacket
Neoprene shoes or sandals with grip
Sleeping bag rated to 0 C
Sun cream and a hat

children.text: Do I need paddling experience?
No. We teach the basics on day 1. You should be able to swim and be happy sitting in a boat for up to two hours at a stretch.
Weather
We decide each morning where it is safe to paddle. If wind keeps us ashore we change the plan and walk instead.

data.title: Ravenhead Lake Kayak Camp
data.summary: Six days on a long mountain lake in British Columbia, paddling by day and camping at the water's edge.
data.intro: Longer paddling days on a lake that can get windy by afternoon. We start early and aim to be off the water by 1 pm.
data.itinerary:
Day 1|Meet at Ravenhead dock at 9 am. Skills session and a short evening paddle.
Day 2|North arm and the first camp. 15 km.
Day 3|To the glacier creek mouth. 18 km. Hike to a viewpoint in the afternoon.
Day 4|Rest or a short paddle to the hot spring pool. 8 km.
Day 5|Return along the east shore. 17 km.
Day 6|Final paddle to the dock by noon, then transfer to Ravenhead town.
data.includes:
Five nights camping (tents and mats provided)
All meals, cooked on camp stoves
Touring kayaks, paddles, spray skirts and buoyancy aids
Two guides for up to eight paddlers
Park camping permits
data.bring:
Warm base layers
Waterproof jacket and trousers
Sleeping bag rated to minus 5 C
Sun hat and polarised sunglasses
Swimsuit for the hot spring day

children.text: Fitness
You should be comfortable being active for six hours a day. Some paddling experience helps but is not required. Tell us when you enquire and we will suggest a short practice session near you.

data.title: Calafque Channels Kayak
data.summary: Eight days weaving between forested islands in southern Chile, with glaciers at the far end.
data.intro: Open channels, strong tides and cold water. This is a trip for confident paddlers who are fit and happy to camp in rain.
data.itinerary:
Day 1|Fly to Puerto Calafque. Meet at 6 pm at the guesthouse.
Day 2|Boat transfer to the put-in. Gear check and a first paddle.
Day 3|Island hopping west. 20 km.
Day 4|Tide-timed crossing of the main channel. 16 km.
Day 5|Forest camp and a day walk to a viewpoint. 8 km paddling.
Day 6|To the glacier face. 18 km.
Day 7|Return paddle. 20 km.
Day 8|Boat transfer and flight connections from Puerto Calafque.
data.includes:
Six nights camping (tents and mats provided)
All meals from dinner on day 1 to breakfast on day 8
Single sea kayaks, drysuits or paddle jackets, spray skirts and buoyancy aids
Two guides for up to six paddlers
Boat transfers at the start and end
data.bring:
Warm thermal base layers
Sleeping bag rated to minus 5 C
Rain jacket and trousers
Warm hat and gloves
Two pairs of dry socks per day

children.text: Experience we ask for
You should have paddled a sea kayak on open water before and be able to do an assisted rescue. If you are not sure, tell us and we will talk it through before you book.
Seasons
Dates are in the southern summer. Expect 5 to 14 C, wind and rain on most days.

data.title: Cerro Pellin Base Camp Trek
data.summary: Twelve days walking to a base camp at the foot of a granite spire, with a rest day and a summit attempt on a nearby peak.
data.intro: A long trip into remote country. You walk with a pack for several days, then base from one camp. A summit attempt is offered to those who are keen and fit, if conditions allow.
data.itinerary:
Day 1|Meet in Rio Pellin town at 5 pm. Kit check.
Day 2|Drive to the trailhead. Walk 6 hours to the first camp.
Days 3 to 5|Valley approach, two river crossings. 6 to 8 hours a day.
Day 6|Arrive at base camp. Afternoon rest.
Day 7|Day walk to the glacier lake. 7 hours.
Day 8|Rest day at base camp.
Day 9|Summit attempt on Pico Gris (3,100 m), starting at 4 am. 12 hours, weather permitting.
Day 10|Spare day for weather or rest.
Days 11 and 12|Walk out and transfer to Rio Pellin.
data.includes:
Eleven nights in tents and one in a town guesthouse
All meals, cooked by the guides and the group
Group tents, mats, stoves and fuel
Helmets, harnesses and crampons for the summit day
Porters carry food and group camp gear, you carry your own kit (about 12 kg)
data.bring:
Mountain boots that take crampons
Sleeping bag rated to minus 10 C
Warm down jacket
Waterproof shell, jacket and trousers
Gloves, two pairs
Trekking poles
A 50 litre pack

children.text: Is this trip for me?
You should have done at least one multi-day trek with a pack before. We ask everyone to fill in a short experience form and we call each person before accepting a booking.
The summit
Summit day is optional. Guides decide on the day, based on weather, snow and how the group is feeling. Not everyone will go up, and that is part of the plan.

data.title: Hohe Marten Ice Ridge
data.summary: Ten days of glacier travel and rock scrambling in the Austrian Alps, with a skills course in the first three days.
data.intro: We teach rope work, crampon use and glacier travel in the first three days, then use them on a three-day traverse. A mountaineering-skills trip for fit people with some hill experience.
data.itinerary:
Day 1|Meet in Martental at 4 pm. Kit check.
Days 2 and 3|Skills on a low glacier: crampons, ice axe, rope teams, crevasse rescue.
Day 4|Walk to the Marten hut. 4 hours.
Days 5 to 7|Three-day traverse with two hut nights. 6 to 9 hours a day.
Day 8|Summit day on the Marten spire (3,350 m), weather permitting.
Day 9|Spare day for weather.
Day 10|Descent to Martental and transfer by 2 pm.
data.includes:
Nine nights: five in huts, four in a village guesthouse
All meals except drinks at huts
Ropes, helmets, harnesses and group safety equipment
Three guides for up to six people (two people per rope team with a guide each)
Glacier skills instruction
data.bring:
Stiff mountain boots
Crampons that fit your boots (we can advise)
Ice axe
Warm jacket and shell
Gloves and a spare pair
Sun cream and glacier glasses

children.text: Who this trip suits
You are fit, enjoy exposed ground and have been on a few multi-day walking trips. We do not expect you to have used a rope before.
Hire
Boots, crampons, axe and harness can be hired locally. Tell us your sizes when you confirm.

data.title: Mount Ledger High Camp
data.summary: Eight days that introduce high-altitude camping and snow skills in the Rockies, with a gentle summit at the end.
data.intro: A first expedition-style trip. We camp at 2,600 m, learn basic snow skills, and walk to the Ledger summit on day 6 if conditions allow. No climbing experience needed.
data.itinerary:
Day 1|Meet in Ledger Creek at 3 pm. Kit check and briefing.
Day 2|Walk to Low Camp. 5 hours, 600 m up.
Day 3|Move up to High Camp. 4 hours. Camp craft session.
Day 4|Snow skills: walking in crampons, using an ice axe, stopping a slide. Half day.
Day 5|Acclimatisation walk to the col. 5 hours.
Day 6|Summit day, 8 to 10 hours, weather permitting.
Day 7|Spare day, then walk down to Low Camp.
Day 8|Walk out and transfer by 1 pm.
data.includes:
Seven nights in tents (Low Camp and High Camp)
All meals, with hot drinks at camp
Group tents, stoves and fuel
Helmets, crampons and ice axes for the snow day
Two guides for up to eight people
data.bring:
Sturdy hiking or mountain boots
Sleeping bag rated to minus 10 C
Warm layers and a down jacket
Waterproof shell
Gloves and warm hat
A 45 litre pack

children.text: Altitude
The highest point is about 3,100 m. Most people feel a little slow and may get a headache. We go up slowly and your guides check in with everyone each evening.
If we cannot summit
The summit is a bonus and not a promise. In poor weather we walk to the col instead and use the time for skills.

data.title: The Alps
data.intro: Hut-to-hut walking and glacier skills in two mountain ranges. Days are long and the food at the huts is good.

data.title: Norway
data.intro: Fjords, plateau walking and sea kayaking on small beaches. Long summer light, cold water and a lot of waterfalls.

data.title: Patagonia
data.intro: Remote trekking and channel kayaking in the southern summer. Wind, rain and long views.

data.title: The Rockies
data.intro: Cabin-based walking, lake paddling and an introduction to high camping, in valleys with plenty of wildlife.

data.title: Pick a trip and a date
data.text: Filter trips by activity and difficulty and read the day-by-day plan. Dates are listed on each trip page. How many places are left changes often, so ask us before you book flights.

data.title: Send an enquiry
data.text: Tell us the trip, the date you prefer, how many are coming and what you have done outdoors before. We reply by email within two working days.

data.title: Talk it through
data.text: We check the trip suits you and answer questions about fitness and gear. A place is held only once we confirm it by email.

data.title: Meet at the start
data.text: About six weeks before, you get a kit list, the meeting point and a short call with your guide. On day 1 the group meets, packs are checked and the trip begins.

data.title: Tomas Aldric

data.title: Priya Lindqvist

data.title: Dario Quell
data.bio: Leads the Patagonia and Rockies expeditions and writes the kit lists for them.

data.title: Hannah Boyd
data.bio: Answers your emails and calls, books huts and transfers, and sends you what you need before departure.
